title: Meaningful Connections Meetup
description:
* Not into small-talk, loud bars, social media and dating apps?
* Enjoy stimulating conversations, challenging yourself, learning new things?

It is a guided event - you won’t be stuck for what to do or what to talk about. Most of the talking will be done 1 on 1 in rotating pairs so you will have an opportunity to interact and connect with 10-15 people and go beyond small talk to get a deeper sense of who they are.

Perfect if you are new in town, a bit socially isolated due to work or circumstances, looking for new friends or someone special, or just want to venture outside of your familiar social circle.

You will have fun, enjoy getting to know new people on a below-the-surface level, learn more about yourself and increase your social skills and confidence.

Who knows, maybe you’ll make a new friend or even a romantic connection - but only if that happens naturally. The main purpose of this afternoon is good company, human connection and stimulating conversation. It is a no-pressure way to meet a bunch of new people.

title: Agentic Engineering Day New Zealand
description:
Hi all,

We’re excited to bring [Agentic Engineering Day to New Zealand](https://www.agenticbuild.day/) this October 21–22, 2026 in Auckland.

Agentic Engineering Day is an independent, community-driven conference for software engineers, architects, builders, and curious minds exploring what it really means to work with AI systems in practice. From agents and emerging standards like MCP, SKILLS, to orchestration, evaluation, governance, observability & tracing, security, memory & context management and infrastructure - this is about the messy, real-world challenges of moving Cognitive Architectures out of the lab and into hardened, reliable production systems.

Whether you're experimenting with your first agent or scaling complex AI systems, this is a space to learn, share, and help shape the future of the local industry - together.

**Note:** Make sure to register to secure your seat! There is limited space available.

**[Agentic Engineering Day](https://www.agenticengineering.day/) (formerly Agentic Build Day)** is a paid event with community-priced tickets. Join us and support!

**Call for papers OPEN!**

If you're building agentic systems, shipping them into production, or pushing the boundaries of what autonomous AI can do, we want to hear about it.

Share what you're learning with the community and let’s build the future of agentic systems together.

Submissions are open now → https://www.agenticengineering.day/

title: Jev, Dots, and more: Automating the Day-to-Day
description:
Running a business means a constant stream of work: follow-ups, research, reporting, triaging requests, routing tickets, scoring leads, chasing details across a dozen apps. Two new tools are aimed squarely at that work.

OpenAI's Dots, launched at DevDay this week, are always-on agents that handle tasks in the background on their own cloud computer.

TypeSafe's Jev, released last month, is a model built for the high-volume decisions inside your systems, returning a choice or score with a confidence level instead of text.

This is a demo and discussion session on what these tools can do for how you operate: what's worth adopting now, what to wait on, and how to tell the difference. Bring the tools you're already using and your opinions.

We'll explore:

* What just shipped. The recent OpenAI announcements and the new TypeSafe model, and what each means for a working business.
* Dots as a coworker. The open-ended work that piles up, such as research, follow-ups and bug triage, and what it looks like to hand it to an always-on agent.
* Jev for decisions inside your process. Routing support requests, scoring leads, flagging invoices and sorting inbound work, with confidence scores that tell you when a human should step in.
* Where to start. How to pick the first process worth automating, and how to measure whether it helped.
* Trust and oversight. Approval rules, confidence thresholds and guardrails for software that acts while you're not watching, and how to test vendor claims yourself.

No prior background assumed. If you run a business, lead a team, or build the systems they rely on, this is for you.
Afterwards we usually continue over dinner nearby, a good chance to connect with fellow builders and practitioners.
